title: Krylov Tomography and Finite-Uncertainty Certification of Exceptional-Point Dynamics
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) can produce striking responses, but locating one does not reveal how much of its dynamics an excitation accesses, which responses a detector distinguishes, or whether a missing signal is absent or undetected. We introduce Krylov tomography, a preparation- and measurement-aware framework that uses time-resolved data and models with stated uncertainty limits to answer these questions, while also bounding offset-induced departures from exact-EP behavior. As an explicit illustration of the general framework, we present finite-precision simulations of a red-sideband optomechanical model, whose second-moment coherence sector contains a third-order EP, certifying preparation-sensitive access to two and three directions. Krylov tomography thus bridges EP structure and finite-precision measurements, providing a general framework for non-Hermitian systems.
summary: The paper introduces Krylov Tomography, a novel framework that analyzes quantum dynamics near Exceptional Points (EPs) by accounting for preparation and measurement uncertainties. It quantifies the difference between the theoretically available dynamics and the experimentally accessible dynamics. This provides a robust method for certifying the true dynamical structure of non-Hermitian systems using finite-precision measurements.
main_problem: To develop a preparation- and measurement-aware framework to determine the actual dynamics accessed by an excitation near an Exceptional Point (EP), addressing the ambiguity between available Jordan structure, activated depth, and resolved directions.
main_result: The framework successfully separates the available Jordan structure, the activated depth, and the resolved depth, providing the first finite-error certification theory for preparation- and readout-selected Jordan dynamics.
method: Krylov Tomography is employed, using time-resolved data and models with stated uncertainty limits to analyze the evolution of excess moments governed by a linear system.
model_or_system: The analysis is illustrated using a linearized red-sideband cavity-optomechanical model, which is a non-Hermitian system exhibiting an Exceptional Point (EP). The dynamics are analyzed on a closed moment sector.
key_observables: Activated depth ($d_{	ext{act}}$), independently resolved depth ($d_{	ext{rank}}$), and the terminal reopening radius ($R_r$).
important_parameters: Uncertainty bounds ($\epsilon_j$), the EP location, and the coherence norm ($\|v\|_{	ext{coh}}$).
main_assumptions: The method requires independent establishment of the relevant closed sector, the isolated EP contribution, and the detector response, relying on bounding departures from exact EP behavior.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the preparation-evolution-readout structure, linking available, activated, and resolved structure via Krylov tomography, and show preparation-dependent Krylov responses for depth-three and depth-two chains.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the framework by defining the relationship between available, activated, and resolved depth. It then applies this to the optomechanical model, deriving finite-error certification tests for the rank and depth, and finally presents quantitative results for specific preparations.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, quantitative tool to extract the true dynamical structure of non-Hermitian systems near EPs, moving beyond simple eigenvalue analysis by incorporating realistic measurement uncertainties.
